utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. May I ask the registrar to call out the case number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-13a-T, the Prosecutor versus Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. As agreed, we will do without the appearances and we could start right away. [From the OTP: Mr. Niemann, Mr. Williamson, Mr. Waespi, Mr. Vos For the Accused: Mr. Fila, Mr. Petrovic, Mr. Kostic] Mr. Fila, our next witness is Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lazarevic. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, did you speak with the investigator from the Fila office, lawyer Miroslav Vasic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please look if this is your statement and whether you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D82, the English translation D82A.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is that the statement, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If there are no remarks, Defence suggests this is submitted as evidence, D82.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I see there is no objection from the Prosecution. Yes, it is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, did you graduate from law school in Belgrade and when?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Upon my arrival in Kladovo, I was employed as the Chief of the Secretariat at the Assembly of the Municipality, then I was President of the Municipality. After that, I was director of the company, Termoment (phoen) near Kladovo. After leaving Kladovo, right now, I am director of the firm, Solidano (phoen) that's part of the electoral distribution network of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In which period were you President of the Municipal Assembly of Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was elected on November 27th, 1989, and I was at that post until June 27th of '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: We're interested in the period of November 20th, '91. So I would like to ask you whether, on that day, you saw Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The day before, did you -- where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I slept in the house of Slavko Dokmanovic in Trpinja with Mr. Jovan Cvetkovic and my driver, Dragan Ivezic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So that's the night between the 19th and 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please play the tape now, which is the Defence Exhibit D2, from the start of the tape, so when you see yourself, you will say "This is me," and then we will go on to the tape. (Videotape played) Do you see yourself?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who are the people that you see?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Ljoba Novakovic, President of Backa Palanka. This is Mirko Dragisic, Rade Simic, Mita Lolic, Djordje Milivojevic, Drago Ljubaliksic (phoen), Rade Simic, Visa Maletic, Tomic, Slavko Dokmanovic, Jova Cvetkovic. Slavko Dokmanovic. Mita Lolic. Slavko Dokmanovic. Mirko Dragisic. This is me. Rade Leskovac. Djordje Milivojevic, the director from Backa Palanka. Dusan Niculovic, Boris Ivaskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I suggest that you look at the photographs, and if you tell us if you are on any of these photographs. And if you are, you will tell us which ones. The photographs are not too good, but the technical capabilities are bad in Yugoslavia. We don't have the ability. Are you on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Dokmanovic, Mita Lolic, Mirko Dragijic, and myself. So the four of us looking from this side, from the left to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please tell us now how you found yourself in Backa Palanka when the photograph was taken; what were you doing there? How did you get there? Why? With whom did you get there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The previous agreement was to make a delegation to go to Vukovar to take humanitarian aid, but since I was friends with Mr. Ljuba Novakovic and we worked in Backa Palanka and Kladovo, I set the place for where we were to meet because Backa Palanka is a place on the Danube, so that's the closest place to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. How did you get there on the evening of the 19th and with whom?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Dokmanovic. On the 19th in the evening at Slavko Dokmanovic's, I came with my driver, Dragan Ivezic, and we spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When did you leave in the morning and who did you leave with and when did you arrive at Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I had to leave earlier because of a prior meeting with businessmen from Backa Palanka, so at six in the morning, I left Slavko Dokmanovic's house with my driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When did you get to Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Around eight o'clock in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So Slavko got there later?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In Backa Palanka, you were until when, approximately?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After an informal talk, it was around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So until about noon. And then you left where?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We went towards Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So please continue the tape now. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Stop. This picture that you saw just now, could you play it back in order to see this photograph. It's around 12 noon, from there, if you can play the tape? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. Who is in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Myself, Mr. Rade Leskovac, and a soldier, I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you look at this photo, but only when the court sees it. Then you can say whether you are on that photograph and whether that's it. Is that the time when you are leaving and is that the place in front of the Municipal Assembly of Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is in front of the entrance to the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So is that about the time you're getting ready to leave?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's when we're getting ready to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. You can run the tape. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What is this bridge that you are crossing?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: From Ilok?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, this is on the way out from Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This is what we're watching now.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is Tovarnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who is this now? What is this?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the road towards VELEPROMET.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So it's Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The outskirts of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the outskirts of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where are we now?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We're in the yard of VELEPROMET.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who are these people here? Who is this?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Kosic, Lazarevic, and Tomasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let the tape run. Who are these people?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic and Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan and in the back Slavko Dokmanovic. This is Jaksic and Kosic, Jovan Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This is all in the yard at VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is this the yard at VELEPROMET still?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These are people who at that time were in the yard of VELEPROMET.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were there soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Journalists, I think of Swiss television.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And this?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Goran Hadzic, Mr. Goran Pirocanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Stop. Would you look at these photographs now and tell us if you are on them?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D85.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Are you depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it's time to ask you something. You left Backa Palanka at the time we mentioned. Would you tell us what you left in, who was in which car, how many cars? What happened from Backa Palanka until you got to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From the yard of VELEPROMET --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, not from VELEPROMET, from Backa Palanka when you are leaving at noon towards Vukovar. What is the group?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We left in one car. We divided ourselves into three groups. One delegation in Lada Niva with Mr. Jovan Cvetkovic, myself and Mr. Slavko Dokmanovic and Zoran Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who was driving?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovan Cvetkovic was driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Go on?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the other car was my driver with the municipality's official car with Mr. Mirko Dragisic and journalist Vukosav Tomasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And the third vehicle?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The third vehicle was Mr. Rade Leskovac. That was his private car.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We went towards Vukovar and we entered VELEPROMET around two o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So you arrived with three cars or something happened en route?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: En route, Mr. Rade Leskovac had a flat tyre, so we had to stop. Mr. Rade Leskovac then came into our car with Slavko Dokmanovic, Zoran Leskovac and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So there was five of you then. So that is how you entered into VELEPROMET then? Wait for ten seconds before you respond. We stopped the tape, as you saw in the photograph, around 14.29 where you recognised yourself. In that time, are you in the yard of VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Describe the yard for us, where it is? When you come in, do you pass a gate?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And ...

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The car was in front of the gate. It was an iron gate, a door towards the left when you come in on the left side is the building, and then there were some hangers, so all the time, when -- in VELEPROMET we were outside. That's where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm talking about the people who came?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirko Dragisic, Mr. Jevtovic, Rade Leskovac, Mr. Slavko Dokmanovic and Jovan Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: At one moment Slavko Dokmanovic is no longer there in the yard. What happened?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Dokmanovic entered the building for a government meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How many entrances does that building have?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The building on the left only has one entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And how long did Slavko stay there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We waited for him outside, so all the time we were there, maybe until about three o'clock, which is how long the meeting lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could he have left the building without you seeing him?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Around three o'clock, so later, you are then going where?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We're going towards the centre of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Play the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Explain to us what happens. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May I comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is outside of the building. We are going towards the centre of Vukovar. Yes. This is descending into the centre of Vukovar. These are comments in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you hear Slavko Dokmanovic's voice, say "Now Slavko Dokmanovic is speaking," not what he's saying, just that he's speaking.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That was his voice now. Slavko. This is Rade Leskovac. Slavko's voice now. This is Slavko. Slavko. Slavko's voice still. Slavko's voice. Slavko. Slavko is still commenting. Slavko. Slavko. Slavko still.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where is this now?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is as far as you could pass near the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Continue the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Slavko Dokmanovic and Vusko Tomasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who is speaking now?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Stop. Would you please look to see if you are on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D86.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Maybe it's a good time to clear up a few things, Mr. Lazarevic. When you left VELEPROMET, with which car and how did you leave?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The car was Lada Niva with Mr. Jovan Cvetkovic as the driver, Slavko Dokmanovic, Zoran Jevtovic, Rade Leskovac and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And in the second car?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the second car was my driver with Mr. Mirko Dragisic and Vukosav Tomasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You saw the photograph in front of you. At the moment, is that the group that was in the centre of Vukovar where it was taped?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where are you sitting in relation to Slavko?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All the time during that journey, I was directly behind Slavko Dokmanovic, so Jovan Cvetkovic sat in the front, Slavko sat in the co-driver's seat, I was sitting in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When did you leave from the centre?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Around 3.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you left from VELEPROMET, all the time were you together with Slavko Dokmanovic, practically in the car behind Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could he have gone somewhere without you seeing him?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely impossible. Impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where did you leave later from the centre of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We were going towards Sidski Banovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you stop along the way?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How many times and where?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We stopped twice. The first time, it was in front of Negoslavci, and the second time near Orolik.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Why the first time and why the second time?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first time we were stopped by the police because we caught up with a column of buses and vehicles in front of us and we wanted to pass them, but the police stopped us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Wait. The first time, did you leave the car?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. So the first time, you were stopped by the police, you don't leave the car?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Slavko Dokmanovic neither?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. Then you go on. The second time, where were you stopped?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This was on the barrier near Orolik where we were stopped by the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Between those two stops, did you turn from the road, left, right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you were stopped by the military police in Orolik, what happens?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There was a barrier near Orolik. We were stopped by the military police, and there was an incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please describe that in detail as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Simply because there was a lot of traffic, we wanted to pass. We were allowed to pass first, but the military policeman did not let us pass then. He didn't let us go further. Then, Mr. Slavko Dokmanovic and Rade Leskovac intervened for us to be able to pass. That didn't help. Then there was a conflict where weapons were pointed at the whole group. They took their weapons out, they pointed their weapons towards our groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This was on the side of the army?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment, we all left the car. Rade and Slavko were arguing with the police officers. I had a verbal duel on the other side with another police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was this a military police officer or regular police officer?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Military police officer. At the end, later, Mr. Jovan Cvetkovic came out. We asked the Colonel if we could -- they didn't let us, then they let us. Then the military police officer and several of them, when they noticed the insignia on Mr. Cvetkovic, the captain's insignia on his uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter didn't hear the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you passed Orolik, you're going towards Sidski Banovci. When did you get there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Sidski Banovci around 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My group, my delegation stayed there for maybe about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And during that time, Slavko Dokmanovic was with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What happens with him after that? What happens with you? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After saying good-bye, our delegation goes toward Kladovo, goes towards home.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You say good-bye to Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I want to ask you now: All the time from VELEPROMET until you arrived in Sidski Banovci, was Slavko Dokmanovic with you all the time and the other four?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was there any time where he ran off somewhere to do something maybe for five, ten, or more minutes without you seeing him?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I was directly behind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In the car?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of clothes he wore that day?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What kind of clothes?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He had a camouflage hunting uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is this a JNA uniform?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you take a look at this and could you tell us whether that's it? D48, please. Could you please take a look and tell us whether that is what Slavko Dokmanovic wore that day? If you cannot recognise something, it's all right. You don't have to recognise it. Is that what he wore that day?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The vest, the trousers, and the shirt was similar. I can guarantee for the vest and the trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the vest?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a typical hunting vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Are those the colours worn by the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, this is camouflage huntsman's uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did someone perhaps wear this on another continent? Does the military on some other continent where this kind of clothes?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I've never heard anything like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could I just add something; why this is attire worn by huntsmen?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is pockets and this is also where ammunition is worn -- where ammunition is put. So.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So you cannot put a Kalashnikov in here?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, only ammunition for shot guns when you go hunting.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can I just ask you one more thing? We're almost over. The city you can see on the pictures where you're moving -- I mean on the videotape, the centre, VELEPROMET, and all that, are you sure it's Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It's not from some other continent, another town?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It's not Dresden, for example?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is it perhaps an American town?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Australian?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: New Zealand perhaps?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Interesting. It's interesting how you guess that this was Vukovar because there was a problem yesterday because some people could not remember that this was Vukovar. It was quite simple. Why? Because you were there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you explain now how come this tape was filmed in the first place and why this was done, who filmed it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was filmed by Mr. Zoran Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That is the Director of Radio Djerdap and a journalist from Radio Djerdap. He is also a friend of mine so I asked him because I was going to Vukovar and I wanted to have a memento of this visit and I wanted to have it on film.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who was important then for Jevtovic at that time when he was filming it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The delegation from Kladovo, that was most important. I mean this is the delegation that I led from Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What was the delegation from Kladovo doing there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We went there to take humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In Backa Palanka, did you split up, did some people stay in Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we split up.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Why did you split up?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Simply one part of my delegation went to visit our reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who? Who? Who? Who are these people? I mean these people who are here now in The Hague with you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Doran Mitsolovic (phoen), the driver, Djordje Milivojevic, Visa Maletic, Boris Ivaskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How much time did they spend with Slavko Dokmanovic in Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: An hour or two. Well, we agreed to meet in Backa Palanka after eight, so from eight until noon, about four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You were together in Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were together in Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was Slavko with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: (No answer).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The tape that you saw right now, how did I obtain this tape, this videotape? How did I get it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When Zoran Jetovic came to Kladovo, that is to say a few days after the tape was filmed, Zoran made a copy of it and gave it to me and then I sent copies of this tape to the people who are on the tape so that they would have it as a memento for their archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you send it to Tomasevic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I sent it to Jovan Cvetkovic, Vukosav Tomasevic in Prijepolje and the people who are from Kladovo, they got copies in Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was this in 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And of course at that time you knew that the Tribunal would be established in The Hague in '93?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You didn't know it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And you also knew there would be some kind of Toma Fila on day, who would need this tape in 1997?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You are saying this was an authentic tape that was filmed in 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What you saw now on the screen, is that the tape that you had then?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I just want to ask you something else in this connection. How long have you known Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have known Slavko Dokmanovic since 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How did you get to meet him? Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At that time, Slavko Dokmanovic was President of the Municipality of Vukovar, and I was the President of Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Of the Assembly, the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of the Municipal Assembly. And meeting of the representatives of Danubian countries was organised in Belgrade on the 15th and 16th of May, 1990, I represented Kladovo and Slavko represented Vukovar and that is the beginning of our friendship.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: After that, did you meet him again, afterwards, in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How many times? Were there any parties, for example, or how come did you meet?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had a very good working relationship and Slavko also came to Kladovo to stay with me as my friend. He even attended my wedding when I got married.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know his family too?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Does he have a wife, for example?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know his family, I know his wife, Danuka, his daughter, his granddaughter, I know his son Vlad, I know his brother, I know the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where did they live?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They live in the village of Trpinja, not far from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You're sure this is the village of Trpinja, not far away from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there countless numbers of times. I would spend the night at that house, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you know of the reputation that that man enjoyed?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From many countless conversations I had with his family members, with his neighbours, with his relatives, with his associates in the municipality, I knew that everyone had a very favourable opinion of him as a man. First of all, as a person who was employed in that institution, good and caring husband, parent, grandfather, an exemplary person who lived in that village. You could hear only the best about Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What was your impression? Was this an aggressive man? Is he a man who is capable of doing something that is contrary to Yugoslav norms, our norms? I don't know about foreign norms, but our norms of friendship, of being a good person, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For all this time that I've known Slavko Dokmanovic, it's impossible that he could have done anything like that. He never would have thought of anything like this. I mean, he certainly is not an evil man with ill intentions. I mean, he is a quiet family man, hard-working.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the Prosecutor of this Tribunal has indicted him for being responsible in the killing of 200 innocent people and played a key role in that. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is absolutely untrue and impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, who made the decision for you to go to Vukovar on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The decision to go to Vukovar and to give humanitarian aid to our assistance was passed by our executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this a decision that was made in concert with a number of municipalities in the area, or was it something that was unique to your municipality?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, this was a decision of the Municipal Assembly of Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So other mayors or other presidents of Municipal Assemblies happened to attend Vukovar with similar motives, and that was simply coincidental?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about others. I just know about my delegation and our trip to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And when you went there, you went to see your reservists; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That means people that had come from the Kladovo area?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These were reservists from the area of the Municipality of Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: These are people who had been called up as a consequence of the conflict in Vukovar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Reservists from Kladovo up to the age of 50, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And they were members of the JNA, were they?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And you yourself weren't called up?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, when you went to, first of all, to Backa Palanka -- and I think you went there on the day before the 19th -- did you --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Objection. He never said that he went to Backa Palanka on the 19th. On the 19th, he spent the night in Trpinja at Slavko Dokmanovic's place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It is for the witness to say "Yes" or "No".

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But he said that. The Prosecutor is saying that he said that he was in Backa Palanka on the 19th. That is what the Prosecutor is saying, but that is not what the witness said. The witness said that he was in Trpinja on the 19th. Play the transcript back and you'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. But I think that the witness is capable of saying that he didn't say what the Prosecutor allegedly is attributing to him. I wonder whether the Prosecutor may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll clarify that point then. When did you set out on your journey to Eastern Slavonia in order to make the visit to the reservists? When did you start that journey from Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I left Kladovo a day earlier with my driver on the 19th of November, and I spent the night, that evening, the 19th at Slavko Dokmanovic's place, and the other part of my delegation arrived the next morning, on the 20th, in Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the day, the 19th, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 19th, I went to Trpinja to Slavko Dokmanovic's house with Mr. Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And did you meet Mr. Dokmanovic on the 19th apart from at his place in Trpinja?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We went to pick up Mr. Cvetkovic at Sidski Banovci, and from Sidski Banovci, we came to Trpinja in the evening by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In order to get from Kladovo to Sidski Banovci, what towns do you have to go through?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When we leave Kladovo, we have to go through Belgrade, the Geldapa (phoen) highway to Belgrade, and then there are two or three different roads, but then we stopped in several places en route. We stopped at several places, but our destination was Sidski Banovci. First we went to Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go via Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I stopped at Backa Palanka at one point, but we just wanted to refuel there, wanted to visit a family friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, you went -- at the stage that you went to -- you set off on the 19th, had you made the decision then to visit Vukovar, that is before you set off on the 19th, had you made a decision to go to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Our task was to take humanitarian aid. We knew that fighting was still going on in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And you didn't realise at that stage that you would be able to go to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't even think about that, getting into Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And where was it intended that you would take your humanitarian aid to the reservists? At what place?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Several places where our reservists were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us where they were?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, part of them were in Trpinja, another part in Ernestinovo, and a smaller part in Laslovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you said you went to pick up Mr. Cvetkovic; is that right? Or you did pick him up?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And why did you decide to do that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, simply we had agreed to do so. I simply wanted to see my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But how did you know to pick him up? What were the arrangements made in order to do that? Was that something that Mr. Dokmanovic had told you about on the 19th or is that something that you discovered independently of Mr. Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We had agreed on that. In Erdut, we decided to visit Jovan Cvetkovic with Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So it was Mr. Dokmanovic's decision, was it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, it was my decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And you knew, obviously, that Mr. Cvetkovic was at Sidski Banovci?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And you knew that independently of what Mr. Dokmanovic would have told you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I said a few minutes ago that it was my decision to go to see Jovan Cvetkovic, but I knew that Mr. Cvetkovic was in Sidski Banovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I knew because before that, we used to see each other, and I know when he decided to go with his reservists to the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why didn't you decide to go with your reservists in the same way as Mr. Cvetkovic did?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetkovic made his own decision, and I admire him for it. But my decision at that point in time was that I could help in other ways if I stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And help the reservists.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You could help the reservists in other ways, is my question. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. My function was to be the first among equals in Kladovo, and I thought that when I would work in Kladovo and send this humanitarian aid, that I would be contributing in that way. I had not been mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So when you took the humanitarian aid to the reservists, this was one way of you showing your support for them being engaged in this war.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No, this was simply my duty as President of the Municipal Assembly to come and see my own people, after all, these are our friends, our neighbours, our brothers. So it's not that we are expressing support for someone. This is simply a normal act. This is practice with us in the Municipality of Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you weren't trying to support them; is that what you're saying? I don't understand your answer. You're either there to give them humanitarian aid in support or you didn't.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand -- I mean, what does this mean, this kind of support? I'm sorry, but could you please explain this. What do you mean by "support"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, isn't it a fact that you had reservists from your municipality of Kladovo who were located in the war theatre? That's a fact, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact that you wanted to show solidarity and support with them because of the tasks that they were performing? That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, he is saying "No, no" over there, and I think it's very distracting for him to be making comments when I'm cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, please do refrain from indicating your position. Let us move on. Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So that isn't true. So then why, just tell us why you took this humanitarian aid to the reservists from the Kladovo area if you didn't do it in order to support them and assist them?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Simply we took humanitarian aid, cigarettes, coffee, we took parcels that their families had prepared for them, and this was simply a token of our care in every possible human way. We were trying to help our fellow citizens who were on the front. I mean, this is the way we treated our people who would go to the front or who would come back from the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next day, that's the morning of the 20th, you went to Backa Palanka ahead of Mr. Dokmanovic and you met him at the municipal assembly building in Backa Palanka; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then followed a meeting of a number of gentlemen that we saw on the video who met there at that building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First of all, this was a gathering of friends. This was an informal meeting. I was the only one who had already had a meeting scheduled with a few directors from Backa Palanka, and this was simply a gathering of old buddies and friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm not disputing that. What was discussed at this meeting of old buddies and friends?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Some of these people hadn't seen each other for quite some time, some people had been absent. I had taken care of this -- these economic affairs that I had to handle because, on the one hand, I was supposed to bring this humanitarian aid, and on the other hand, I was supposed to talk to these directors of various companies in Backa Palanka. So these were friends who met after quite some time. We talked about, naturally, family affairs, also what was going on in terms of the war, and also some of us, at least part of my delegation, we were discussing economic affairs too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And in terms of things going on in relation to the war, what did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We were commenting on the situation that prevailed in those days in that area. Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any discussion about what would happen in Vukovar once the conflict had ceased?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify your question to me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you discuss -- was there any discussion about what would happen in Vukovar once the conflict was over and the matter with the place was restored to normal again?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no. The fighting was still on. On that day, we found out that one could enter part of Vukovar, and we weren't really discussing the future of Vukovar, something like that. No mention was made of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And when precisely is it that you found out that you could enter part of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but it was during these conversations there in the assembly of Backa Palanka, I can't tell you the exact time, but during this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And who provided you with this information?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I can't remember now, but someone brought this piece of news into this meeting room where we were sitting. Someone said that one could enter part of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, at this meeting in Backa Palanka, was there anyone armed?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: May I have Exhibit D83? Just looking at the gentleman sitting at the furthest end of the table, right at the top end of the table. Does he have a weapon in his hand?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't really discern faces in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to tell us who it was, I'm simply asking whether the gentleman at the far end is holding a machine gun. I think it's a machine gun.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we could have a look at the video, if we could, and could we start the video at that point, around about 10.36, I think? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Stop. Do you see that gentleman there with something in his hand?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Probably some kind of weapon. Could you play it back? Could you rewind it just a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: By all means, yes. If it could just be played back? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it looks like a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why was it necessary for people to be armed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I answered that none of us wore a weapon, but this is probably a person escorting Colonel Tomic because he was the only one who wore a uniform in addition to Mr. Cvetkovic, so I gather this is someone from Colonel Tomic's escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: While we are with the tape, I think we will deal with it now, if I may? You said that the first stop that you made after you left Vukovar at the end of the day, after you left Vukovar, was at Negoslavci; is that right? That's what you said in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I said that we stopped for the first time somewhere before Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And how much before Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but it was directly before the entrance to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us in terms of metres, how far that would be before you entered Negoslavci? Approximately. I know you didn't measure it, no doubt.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's impossible. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is it an area where there are houses or is it open fields?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think it's -- this is directly before the entrance to Negoslavci, so maybe there were a few houses and then you would go in, so it was directly before the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'll just confirm this on the tape so that it's the same place that we're talking about, if I can? And might the tape be shown right at the very end, 15.36, on the 20th of November? After you leave Vukovar -- well, we're waiting for the tape. After you leave Vukovar, are there any houses between Vukovar and Negoslavci that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, this is in Vukovar, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is going out of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And these are the last houses at Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, this is -- what's this place here? Just stop there, if we may?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is when we met the -- caught up with the column of buses with the people who were being evacuated from VELEPROMET.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And just for the record tell me again where that was.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, as precisely as you can, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I didn't ask you exactly. You said a moment ago it was on the outskirts of Negoslavci, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I said, when you asked when we stopped for the first time, this is the road to Negoslavci. Our first stop was before Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And didn't you say that that was right at the entrance to Negoslavci, your first stop, when you met the buses?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we were stopped by the military -- no, the police, that was the first time before and -- close to Negoslavci, before the entrance to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And that last clip that we saw with the buses, was that the place that you're talking about, or is it somewhere else? This one here that we're looking at. Is this the place we're talking about or was it some place else?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly whether that was the place. Probably that was that part when we were catching up with the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Tell us again: Where was it that you caught up with the buses?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I said exactly at the entrance to Negoslavci, on the road to Sidski Banovci, so somewhere on the road before Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is there some doubt in your mind that this part of the video represents that place where you met up with the buses?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly or remember whether that was that place exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, might the witness be given a copy, the court copy, of the tape, D2, I think it is? Now, Mr. Lazarevic, I'd like you to examine it closely, take it out of its cover and look at it closely. I'm asking you to look at the box in the case and the tape itself. Now, that's the videotape that you received relating to your visit to Vukovar, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, when did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A few days on the return of Zoran Jetovic from Uzice, so a few days after our return to Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you returned on the 21st, you would have been back in Kladovo on the 21st, is that right, or the 20th?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It would be already the 21st, early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And a few days after that, say -- what? -- three days after that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know precisely. A few days on our return. So whether that was three or five days, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So it could have been as few days as three or as many as five?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't say -- I said a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I protest that Mr. Fila is making comments in the course of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Fila turned his back on the Prosecution. If necessary, I'll leave. I'll leave the premises. With the permission of the court, I will leave so that Mr. Niemann could ask his questions. Thank you. And I will leave the gentleman to sit in for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Let us please --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If Mr. Niemann thinks that I am disrupting the questions when my back is turned when he made the remark, I turned my back and I will sit that way throughout the whole process because that's my protest, but I will go out for him until he finishes posing his learned questions and then I will come back. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, please do stay here and, of course, I'm sure that you will go -- you will refrain from making any comments and remarks, it goes without saying, I am sure you will behave quite properly, and I wonder whether Mr. Niemann could continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So it could have been as few as three days or as many as five that you received the tape?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I said it was a few days, so I don't remember. A few days upon the return of Zoran Jetovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I'm just trying to see if you could help me as being as precise as possible as to what you received the tape, that's all, and I'm just asking you if you can think back to then and tell me whether you remember it as being as few as three days or whether it was as many as five?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but I think that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to protest. This is really not okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: ... That the witness is not able to say how many days after his return back home he received this particular tape, so he said a few days. Can we move on to a further question? Clearly he cannot remember precisely the number of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, who made a copy of the tape for you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A copy of the tape was made by Zoran Jetovic, the Director of Radio Djerdap.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And this was the tape that you provided to Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my tape that I gave to the Fila lawyers' office, and this is my handwriting on the back of the tape here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And just finally, just going back to the time you left Vukovar on that day of the 20th of November of 1991, is it your evidence that after you left the centre of Vukovar, you did not stop until you reached the buses? The vehicles did not stop at any stage or make any turns or changes to your trip until you reached the buses which you believe to be somewhere near Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In my previous statement, I said that upon our return on our way out from the centre of Vukovar, we stopped twice: Once was shortly before Negoslavci when we were stopped by the police; the second time we stopped near Orolik. There was never any turning off from the road until Sidski Banovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I would like the witness to see the continuation of the tape on the 28th and explain how it was that the visit on the 20th and 28th is on the same tape because that was the sense of the questions, two, three, five days. Please play the continuation of the tape of the 28th so that we could see how both tapes are on the same tape because that was the sense of the previous questions. (Videotape played) 20

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Please note this tape. What is that? What is this? When was this filmed? When did you receive a copy of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could the witness please answer the question asked by Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This recording from the 28th was made during the visit of the delegation, our delegation, from Kladovo to the workers who were temporarily working abroad who had collected humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you get both of those tapes on this videotape that you have from Zoran Jetovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The visit of the 28th was added to this tape. The visit on the 28th was recorded later and it was added to the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this has been clarified now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, it's really a question for you rather than the witness. We were given at the outset of these proceedings a transcript which related to the tape, and at some stage, it would be helpful to go through that transcript -- it may be during the evidence of your client -- and know who is speaking and when since we have an English translation of it, and at the moment we don't know who is speaking, we have had general evidence about it, but obviously it would be useful to know if it is possible to identify who says what.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to respond right away to that question. It was promised that the Dutch authorities would have expert testimony on this tape, they would check the accuracy of the transcript that I have given you, so in order to avoid me talking, commenting, influencing -- as we have had remarks from the other side -- I wanted the Dutch authorities which cooperate with the Prosecution and not with me to establish the accuracy of the transcript that I guarantee the accuracy. This was done by the Serbian police, the transcript by the Serb police should not be trusted. The Dutch police can be trusted. Unfortunately, Dutch -- the police, in spite of promises from the Prosecution, has done nothing. I am completing my witnesses next week because I have said that in my country, people stick to their word and not to their horns. In French and Latin, I will keep my word, if you wish. If I get this attest as to the accuracy of the tape by Monday, then I could show the transcript on Monday. But in spite of Mr. Williamson's efforts, because he did try to help -- I want to say that -- the Dutch police has still not done this. I would like to have the transcript and we can show it to Mr. Lazarevic and we can play the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to say that we've had nothing to do with any delay associated with this. We merely acted as a conduit to the Dutch police on behalf of the Defence. So any suggestion that there has been no cooperation isn't a consequence of anything we have done. We reject that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If Your Honour -- if you listen to me, I thanked Mr. Williamson just now for his help, so I'm not really -- I am thanking him, but we are not expert witnesses. The Dutch police did not do what it was supposed to do, and Mr. Williamson enabled me to get in contact with them. I don't have a copy of the transcript right now. Maybe we can have a break and then after the break we can do that. I will photocopy the transcript in five copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Maybe we could ask the witness to be so kind as to remain here, so that after the break as suggested by Mr. Fila, we could check the transcript. Now, I wonder whether the Prosecution could insist with the Dutch police that they should cooperate and do what Mr. Fila asked for?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we -- I am in no position to insist on anything with the Dutch police, and we have provided them with the material and they -- I'll ask Mr. Williamson to address Your Honour on the specific details of it -- but as a matter of general principle, we are in no position to insist on anything of the sort. And all we can do is contact them and do it in a timely manner, which we did, and it really should be a matter for Mr. Fila to pursue, not for us. We want to distance ourselves from it and not be involved in it, frankly. It's a Defence matter. But I'll ask Mr. Williamson to give you details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think, to assist, it's not really the accuracy of the tape as far as I know is in dispute, unless there is some point made about it. It's merely, if it's possible to identify who is saying what, particularly what the Defendant says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Which I assume can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can help? Mr. Williamson gave me the contact. We called that person and we found out that he was on vacation until Wednesday. I can't do anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Williamson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we made the initial contacts with the Dutch laboratory just to find out the feasibility of doing these tests. They had indicated that it was a rather labour-intensive process, that they have to take voice samples, and it is not only picking out the voice of Mr. Dokmanovic but they also have to eliminate all of the other voices, so this is, as I understand it, a rather timely process. I communicated that to Ms. Lopicic, we got the tape and forwarded it to the Dutch lab. As Mr. Fila said, the technician that was doing this was on vacation at that time. When the Dutch laboratory called us back to ask questions about it, I then gave that information directly to Ms. Lopicic and suggested she continue the contact directly with them, rather than me being the intermediary and relaying information from both sides. At that time we indicated we would withdraw from the process and that the Defence could communicate directly with them and work out everything. But as Mr. Niemann has indicated, we don't have any particular influence over them, and whether it be for the Defence or the Prosecution, it is, in fact, a favour that the Dutch lab is doing, although they are charging for it so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I even have funds from the registrar, so we've done everything but you can imagine how much influence I have on the Dutch police. A lot. You can imagine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: To take up a point made by Judge May, I think Judge May is right in pointing out that what is in dispute is not the authenticity of this tape, whether or not the tape is authentic. It's a question to verify -- verifying who is saying what. So we could probably -- I wonder whether, after the break, we could try to put names next to voices on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no problem at all, but you will just have to go through the whole tape again. Mr. Lazarevic knows exactly who is speaking when, but you will just have to go through the whole tape again. It is inevitable we have to listen to it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Why not? I mean, if it is in the interests of Mr. Williamson --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: There is no objection from us, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And could use our transcript and --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It's strenuous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. So we have a 20-minute break, we will take a 20-minute break now and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just before you do break. Might I be excused after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. --- Recess at 10.38 a.m. --- Resumed at 10.50 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We have a transcript of the tape in front of us. I wonder whether we could show it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we begin, I have one brief matter that I would like to address the court on. During the break, we have had an opportunity to review the videotape of the proceedings which is made contemporaneously as court progresses. On this tape it is very clear that Mr. Fila suggested an answer to the witness. This is displayed on the tape. We understand that it is impossible to show that now because the tape is continually used for the proceedings. It would, however, be available at the end of the day. Mr. Fila took great exception when we raised this issue, but we feel that this goes to the very integrity of the proceedings and is highly inappropriate behaviour; and therefore, we would suggest that the court view this tape at the end of the day's proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I just want to be quite clear. If this trial -- people are recording what I'm saying to my colleague, Mr. Kostic, I mean, what the Defence attorneys are discussing here, then I would also like to be in a position to see a tape to see what the Prosecutors are doing at the other end, especially when they are laughing while we are putting questions to the witness. I had my back turned to them, and it's quite obvious -- you can see it very nicely on this tape -- I turned my back to the witness when I was talking to Mr. Kostic. I sign their statements, and I don't know where they learned to behave this way. I mean, listening to what the Defence table is discussing, it is impermissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, would you allow us a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The court has decided that both parties should be called upon to refrain from making any comments while the witnesses are being examined or cross-examined. Mr. Fila, please, when you question witnesses, please don't suggest answers or try to refrain from anything which might influence the witness, and the same applies to the Prosecutor. We will move on without going into this --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to explain something. I actually engaged Mr. Kostic because I am not familiar with cross-examination and he is, and I consult him on that. So I turn my back to the witness and I talk to Mr. Kostic. I promise I shall do that in the future too. I turn my back to the witness and I talk to Mr. Kostic, and I believe that that would be sufficient for the purposes of the Prosecutor. So now let us move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just respond very briefly? I understand you have ruled. This was not a question of him speaking with Mr. Kostic. He had his back turned; the question was asked. He turned his head and said "Ne," turned right back. This is clearly evidenced on the tape. This is not a question of us listening in on his conversations or trying to interfere in any way with the carrying on of their defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I did understand what your position was, but I'm sure that Mr. Fila will refrain --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: -- will refrain from making comments, and the same applies to the Prosecutor who, yes, should not sometimes smile or ... Thank you. Let us now try to move on and to get down to business. Could we now go through the tape, and we would ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Please, if possible, could we give the witness a transcript, a copy of the transcript, if it is possible, so that he could follow it too? This is the transcript in Serbian. I mean, there is one in Serbian and there is one in English. The Serbian, please. And, if I understood you correctly, whenever you hear someone speaking, then he says who is the person who is speaking; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, when you hear someone speaking, just say the name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Serbian transcript will be marked as D87.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you want the whole tape or only the part from Vukovar, when they were going from VELEPROMET to Vukovar and then from Vukovar to Sidski Banovci? Do you want only that section, or do you want the part from Backa Palanka too? I think it's not that important, that first part. It was page 6, I think. It would be page 6, if the Prosecutor agrees only to proceed from page 6 onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What I had in mind, there were some comments on the way to Vukovar and going to VELEPROMET. There were some comments -- I think Tovarnik at about 12.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That's right, we start from there, I think -- not from VELEPROMET, from Backa Palanka to Vukovar. I think that. That is twenty past twelve. So please play the tape from twenty past twelve.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you heard that. This is twenty past twelve. That is when you arrive in Tovarnik. Whenever you hear a comment being made, whenever you hear someone's voice, you just say name, "Toma Fila" or whatever. I think the system is quite clear. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is Zoran Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, at what point are we beginning, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is it page --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Again, I turned my back. I wasn't looking. Page 6 of the English version, twelve o'clock. At twelve o'clock, they are in front of Backa Palanka; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We must establish on the English version what is being said as well as in the Serbian. I think it's somewhere near page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If you agree, we can start at the point when they're leaving Backa Palanka. That is the road to Tovarnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But we have got to trace this particular point on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can proceed in the following way, if Your Honours agree? At 10.39, you have in the transcript our handwriting saying Slavko Dokmanovic speaking. That is page 3 of "SD: I respect that." Page 3 of the English transcript. That is 10.39. Can we start from there? So please play the tape from 10.39, please? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Slavko.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And other persons. Whoever's voice you recognise.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That is the voice of Dragoljub Aleksic, the President of Vrsac. That's my voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: What we want to know is who is saying what. So if he can probably, when the tape has a few words, then he says, "This is me saying this." Could he probably say the first few words so that we can identify on the transcript the relevant parts?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Please rewind the tape to the beginning, and you say what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This, of course, applies also to what other people are saying. When he identifies, for instance, Dokmanovic, say the first few words so that we can pinpoint on the transcript the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You repeat the first words that he says so that they can see and then you start by what I say. Play the tape.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Mirko, look at this over here." Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's the top paragraph of page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. Line 7 from above, line 7 from above. Do you want the witness to identify only himself or everyone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Everyone? Play the tape further on, please. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Jova Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Reported ... the goals." Slavko.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What's he saying?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "And look at what he looks like now." Rade Leskovac: "Here, we go left here."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Rade Leskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What is he saying?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Well, there is, there is also ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
