utterances.text: "Take four soldiers and come here." I can't recognise the voice. It is someone in VELEPROMET. One of our people. Stop. Rade Leskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What does he say?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Look at Arkan." Zoran Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What is he saying?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "It might be more important to record the ones down here."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. Rade Leskovac: "What?"

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. Slavko.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What does he say?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The Captain is Jova Cvetkovic, a people's deputy from Svetozarevo." Continue. Stop. Jaksic: "From Svetozarevo?" Continue. Jaksic: "How could I not know you?" "Welcome." That was Jaksic. Continue. Stop. Slavko: "A volunteer in Banovci, will you look at that!" All right. Continue. "People's deputy." Slavko. Continue. I'm sorry. Could we just rewind the tape a bit? Please rewind the tape. Make -- rewind it. A bit more. A bit more. That's it. The previous sentence was mine: "Then we'll make pictures of them later."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Please play the tape further. This is page 6. Page 6, paragraph 2. Play the tape.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. "Slow on. Keep it a bit." That was Mirko Dragisic. Stop. Rade Leskovac: "Let's get into the car and go."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Stop. This is page 6, the penultimate paragraph in the English text. Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: "This is Boro's house." Go on, go on. Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: "It's there." Say it. "Fuck him." Let's go -- stop. Slavko Dokmanovic a bit before that: "Well we are going to see a little." That's okay. Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: "We are going to see a little" -- no, Jova Cvetkovic. "Well we are going to see a little." One, two, three, four, fourth line. Slavko Dokmanovic and Rade Leskovac after him: "No, no, no. That is Paunovic's. That belongs to a Serb, a very rich man from before the war."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who said that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Slavko and Rade Leskovac together. "No, no. A family church." Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. "Oh, a family church." Jova Cvetkovic. Please, please. "No, no. A family church." Can we continue from that point? No, could you rewind it a bit more than that? That's okay. Just let the tape play. Stop. "These houses were Ustashe. Every last one of them Ustashe. This one here is Pivanda's." Slavko Dokmanovic. Slavko. After Slavko, "Folks, I could not imagine this in my dreams," that was Rade Leskovac. Go on. Slavko Dokmanovic's voice saying -- it's not in the transcript, but it says: "It was built without a permit." Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: "This man is doing his best to try to make this functional, look at it!" Stop. "Look!" And then a cuss word. That was Zoran Jevtovic. Stop. Rade Leskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Saying what?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "People...!!!"

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. "People, is that possible?!" Rade Leskovac. Stop. "Well, look! Horror and terror." Cuss word. Jova Cvetkovic. Stop. Jova Cvetkovic: "Not even Stalingrad looked like this." Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic. Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: "Unbelievable! This is that Jovica's house. Lukic. They killed him." Stop. "Look at this." Jova Cvetkovic. Go on. Stop. Rade Leskovac: "God Almighty!" Stop. "Look at little Zoki. My Zoki!" Slavko Dokmanovic. Stop. "This which the camera records ..." Rade Leskovac. Stop. Slavko: "And this, this is the Serbian church. They burned it and they destroyed it. Before it ..." Stop. Mr. Rade Leskovac: "Fuck their Ustashe mother a thousand times. Theirs and Tudjman's!" Stop. Jova Cvetkovic saying: "Look!" Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: "The world has never seen anything like this." Stop. The voice of Slavko Dokmanovic: "Not even that ..." And then the voice of Rade Leskovac. Stop. "Anhajn." Slavko. Stop. "God Almighty" twice, Rade Leskovac. Stop. "There's a corpse! There's a corpse! Look, tape it!" That's Rade Leskovac. And then beneath that, "Eyes were gouged out, hey!" Rade Leskovac. Stop. "There is another one, there." Mirko Dragisic. Stop. "Their Ustashe mother!" et cetera, Rade Leskovac. Stop. "Come on, record this." That is the voice of my driver, Dragan Ivezic. Stop. "Guys, there are many corpses here." Rade Leskovac. Stop. Zoran Jevtovic: "I am coming, I just want to record how destroyed the town is." Stop. "Don't touch it. It smells!" Zoran Jevtovic. Stop. Slavko: "... one great sorrow, not only over the town, but also over thousands of dead and innocent people." Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Whose voice is this now?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "... that lived to see the same fate as 50 years ago, to be killed, slaughtered for no reason ... corpses." That's Slavko's voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That's Slavko, the entire paragraph?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. "The others will be left with memories only." That is Slavko. And before that, all of that was Slavko. So say the whole thing. "It is all so horrible. It must be most difficult for those who lost their dearest. The others will be left with only memories."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That is Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. Slavko: "People are recovering from everything and we hope that Vukovar and its people ..." Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. Slavko: " ... after 50 years and not to let anything like this happen again anywhere ever." Go on. Stop. This is the voice of Slavko Dokmanovic: "It certainly will not be in Vukovar, because from this day to eternity Vukovar will be Serbian." Go on. Stop. Zoran Jevtovic: "And this is shooting that is going on over there? Pockets?" Stop, stop. "Oh, fuck, what do these ..." Slavko. Stop. "This is the first time I see a man with his throat cut." Rade Leskovac. Stop. "Those are theirs. That army doesn't slaughter like that." Jova Cvetkovic. Stop, stop, stop. Could you just rewind it a little bit, if possible? More. Stop, stop. "And who knows who it is now?" Slavko Dokmanovic. Stop, stop. Rade Leskovac: "What's that, theirs?" Stop. "Yes, our guys are ..." Jova Cvetkovic. Stop, stop. "Each settlement is like this." Slavko. Rewind the tape, please. The text isn't okay. Now. Stop. Just a bit more. Just rewind it a bit more, please? Now. Stop. "What's that, theirs?" That's Rade Leskovac. And then ... now listen. "Is she alive?" That is Rade Leskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Once again, please, before Rade Leskovac, who is speaking before Rade Leskovac?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you put up the volume, please? Stop. This is the voice of Slavko Dokmanovic: "Get the dredge immediately and load."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. This is Zoran Jevtovic: "All of this has to be torn down." Stop, stop, stop. "Torn down? OK, that does not necessarily mean ..." Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That is page 10 of the transcript; you know that.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. This is the voice of Slavko Dokmanovic: "This is how it was, this man just fixed it ..." Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: " ... and was about to open the production and they destroyed it." Stop. "It will be fixed." Slavko. Stop. Slavko's voice: "Here, this is what the police station ..." Stop. "Here, this is what the police station in Dalj was like." Slavko Dokmanovic. Stop. Slavko Dokmanovic: "But these were all Ustashe houses." Go on. Stop, stop. "That is the International Red Cross." Rade Leskovac. Go on. Stop. Jova Cvetkovic: "They should not see these thieves carrying the bags." Stop, stop. Rade Leskovac: "Well, let's go and see." Stop, stop. Leskovac: "Don't!... We don't want anything." Slavko Dokmanovic: "We don't want what?"

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Stop. Well, wait for the end of the sentence. Go on.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Stop. "Don't!... We don't want anything. We know what it looks like. What's the point?!" Slavko Dokmanovic. Stop. Jova Cvetkovic: "Look at these trees, how every tree is hit," et cetera. Go on. Stop. "And what is that there?" That is the voice of Jova Cvetkovic. Stop. That was Slavko Dokmanovic. Stop. "Did they, my mother Jovo, what do you think?" Slavko Dokmanovic. Go on. Play the tape until the end. Stop. "Well, how would they not know me?" Slavko Dokmanovic. Go on. Rade Leskovac at the end saying: "Ah, oh."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a quick question: What was the last thing that he said Mr. Leskovac said at the very end? We didn't catch that. Perhaps you could rerun?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Rewind the tape, please. He's saying "Ah, oh." You can't really translate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very substantive statement. That will be all, Your Honour. I suggest that the transcript be admitted as evidence, Defence Exhibit -- I don't know the number. Transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D87, and the English translation, D87A.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: We have another witness, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I have just one question and then I'm afraid we have to break at a quarter to twelve. Mr. Lazarevic, at one point we saw you next to Arkan. Did you have the chance of talking to him?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a few sentences, "How are you? What are you doing?" when he walked up to us when we were in VELEPROMET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Did you know why he was there, the purpose of his presence there at VELEPROMET in the yard?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know because he showed up all of a sudden. I saw him when he walked in. Neither why nor what for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You didn't ask yourself why he was there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume there is no objection to the witness being released? Mr. Lazarevic, thank you so much for coming here to give evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. (Witness stood down)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will break now, and as I suggested, we will start again at 3.00. I apologise for this long break. And from 3.00 to 6.00. Thank you. --- Luncheon break at 11.40 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25 --- Upon resuming at 3.00 p.m. (The accused entered court) (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I ask you to make the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Dragisic, did you have a conversation with the investigator from the Fila Vasic office? Would you please look at the statement and tell us whether that is yours?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D88 and the English translation D88A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. Fila, please. I am having some trouble with this machine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is that your statement? If there are no objections, I submit it as evidence for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Dragisic, which university have you finished, where and when?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I completed the university of chemistry (sic) in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where were you employed later and where are you employed now?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: For the past 20 years, I've been working in Kladovo; and before that, I was working in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What are you doing in Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I am the director of the musical and elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So you're a professor, a director of a school?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Dragisic, you are under oath. You are teaching our kids, I hope, honesty and humanity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes. In any case, this is my holy or sacred pedagogic vow.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Everything that I'm asking you, please respond in the same way that you would be respond when you are bringing up kids.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were you in the delegation of the Municipality of Kladovo that went to visit the war area on November 20th, '91?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Why were you in that delegation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: There are two main reasons: Because I was there to visit my former students whose director I was and, at the same time, to visit the athletes who were there as reservists because I was then the president of the soccer club.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The reservists, you mean the people who are mobilised in the JNA; these were not volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, no. These were people who were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When did you arrive to Backa Palanka and why, particularly, to Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We got to Backa Palanka around 8.30, and the reason was because the President of the Municipal Assembly of Kladovo, Lazarevic, was there, and he was also the President of the Municipal Assembly of Backa Palanka, Novakovic, and he was also a partner in business, so we got there because -- based on their friendship and their acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who did you arrive to Backa Palanka with, you personally, I mean?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Personally, I came to Backa Palanka with a driver. We were driven by driver Jevtovic. I was with him in Belgrade. We picked up -- we called him Korea, we called him Korea. I can't remember his last name. Perhaps it was Tomasevic -- yes, Tomasevic. We call him Korea, so that's the usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So the three of you came together on the 20th of November in the morning to Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In Backa Palanka, did you see Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you see him anywhere in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: In the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Point to him. How long have you known Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I know him from Lazarevic's wedding because he was at the wedding. Both of us were there at the Lazarevic wedding. That's where we met one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Please play the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Dragisic, you will see the tape from Backa Palanka, so tell us when you will be able to see yourself. I don't have any signal. There is a problem, technical problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, we will have to wait a few minutes, about ten minutes, to show the videotape. I wonder whether you could ask questions while we are waiting for the videotape to be repaired?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You know Slavko Dokmanovic, you said, from the wedding.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you saw him -- then you saw him in Backa Palanka; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: For the second time in Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And the first time in Kladovo at the wedding and the second time in Backa Palanka. How long did you stay in Backa Palanka, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We stayed there approximately until twelve o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Then you left there. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We left towards the direction of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can you tell us who went and how?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: It was like this: There were three cars. There was a Mercedes that Leskovac left and there was a Lada in which there was Dokmanovic, Cvetkovic, Jevtovic and Lazarevic, and also there was a driver with me, Ivaskovic and Tomasevic who we call "Korea" and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you left Kladovo for Backa-- when you left Kladovo for Palanka, did you plan to go to Vukovar. When was the decision made?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: The decision was made in Backa Palanka while we talked about all kinds of things, about the events that were happening in the environs, the circumstances, the situation, and I was told that Vukovar has been pretty destroyed, it's been liberated, and that even it can be seen if we wanted to, of course we wanted to, so that's where we went for these very reasons that I've stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Just one moment. Would you please repeat again who was in the car that you were in from when you were leaving from Backa Palanka in the car that you were in, who else was in that car?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: The car, Tomasevic, myself, and, of course, Ivezic, yes, that's the driver, Ivezic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you left Backa Palanka, then at one point you arrive in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: After a certain period?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where did you get to when you entered Vukovar? Where did you stop off at?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We stopped off at a business. As far as I remember, it was at the entrance to Vukovar, it was a business organisation on the entrance to Vukovar, it was on the left side, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is that perhaps called VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's called VELEPROMET. Later I found out that it was called VELEPROMET.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you got to VELEPROMET, did you all get there at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: With how many vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Three -- no, sorry, we arrived in Vukovar with two vehicles because in the meantime, there was a breakdown of the Mercedes so that he moved to the Lada.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who do you mean by "he"?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Leskovac. He moved to the Lada so that we arrived in Vukovar in two vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So then you arrived in VELEPROMET and you were in the yard of VELEPROMET.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where you were standing in the yard in VELEPROMET? We will see this later in the tape.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Mostly I stood in front of the building itself, close to the entrance, close to the guard house. I was curious because I'm a pedagogue, an educator and a chemist as well, I was looking at the world, I was watching the situation, so most of the time I spent at the entrance to the gate next to the guard house.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. So can we play the tape now? I hear that it's been fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The tape from Backa Palanka). (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you see yourself, please indicate that. You have the tape?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, I don't have the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: He is not switched on properly. Please return the tape to the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. From there. Can you see the tape now? Run the tape. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: This is me. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and to look at these pictures and to tell me whether it is you on these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me -- oh, I'm looking at the video monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D89.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Play the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Once again, when you see yourself, stop us. Please run the tape.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: This is me again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who is this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: That is Korea and this is the driver who was driving us. This is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please look at these photographs to see if you are depicted on them?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph is marked D90.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please play the tape from the moment they enter VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you see yourself, if you see yourself, please point to where you are. Is that VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I saw myself a little earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. You can continue. Would you look at this photograph and tell us whether that is you? Move the tape a little forward to 14.29. That's good. Is that you on the photograph? Would you look at the photograph first and then say?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph is marked D91.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Run the tape, please. Stop. Play it back -- rewind a little bit, please. Would you please ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please tell us whether you are on that photo?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you wait until everybody gets the photos?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D92.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you rewind the tape to 15.05 where the witness was standing so that he can identify himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where are you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I'm at the entrance and exit gate by the guard house.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Of VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What were you doing at the gate?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I was watching. I was watching everything that was happening. There was a lot of people. People were going in and out. That's what I was looking at from professional curiosity.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So that's the gate on the right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did Slavko Dokmanovic pass that way? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So can we conclude that he didn't pass?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where do you go from VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: From VELEPROMET we go towards the centre of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How did you go? Which vehicle? Who is in which vehicle and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Same composition that we arrived in. In the front is the Lada with Dokmanovic, Lazarevic, Cvetkovic, Jevtovic, and in the other car, Tomasevic, Ivezic, the driver, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where was Leskovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Leskovac was with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In the Lada Niva?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where are you going?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We're going towards the centre of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Why are you only leaving just then? Were you waiting for somebody?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were waiting for Dokmanovic. He had some obligations there so we waited until he finished with those obligations and then he joined us and went with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where did he have those obligations physically?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Physically in the office, on the premises which were very close to the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is there only one entrance door to there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a ground floor, one-storey building with one entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So you waited for him in order to go towards the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Then you go to the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you stay when you came to the centre of the town, did you leave the car?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you recognise your voice?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please play the tape so we can hear his voice? (Videotape played) Rewind the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is that you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: A bit more. Yes, I can recognise myself there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Then ...

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Stop, stop. That's me. That's me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. Go on. But did you manage to hear your voice?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. But you recognised your face?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Oh, absolutely. That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now you've come to the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And you stayed there for a certain period of time and then you set off for some other place out of the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We started moving in the direction of Kladovo where we came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In the direction of Kladovo. That's far away, you know. Before that, you went in another direction, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. The same place that we came from, Backa Palanka, the direction of Backa Palanka, but we stopped at a house where Cvetkovic was staying, we all stopped there, the same group of people, the same way. We all wanted to have a glass of homemade brandy and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you were leaving the centre of Vukovar --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: -- before you reached Sidski Banovci where Cvetkovic was, did you stop somewhere in the meantime and for how long?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes. To the best of my knowledge, two, because we encountered a column of those buses and vehicles with civilians. There were some problems there because we tried to overtake them and they stopped them and then we were stopped again by the army. At the same time, they had some kind of regime of movement of their own. We reacted a bit to that, but they were a bit more energetic, they even pointed their arms at us saying that we would have to observe certain standards, certain rules. We got out there, we all smoked a cigarette -- we all smoked cigarettes respectively, then Cvetkovic got out and the whole thing was pacified --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know what the name of this place was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, it was the first time I was there ever. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else. When you set out from Vukovar, when you start the first time and then the second time and then later, you arrived at the town where Jovan Cvetkovic was staying, did you make any detours from that road?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were you driving behind the Lada Niva all the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The one in which Dokmanovic, Jovan, and these other people were?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And that remained identical until you arrived in Banovci?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This Lada Niva, did it manage to turn somewhere else to get out of your sight?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. They were in front of us all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you see if they turned somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Oh, definitely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So you went wherever they went?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, we went wherever they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So it was eight of you, if I'm not mistaken, and together you arrived in Sidski Banovci?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, some kind of village, I don't know. Probably Sidski Banovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where Jovan Cvetkovic was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: That's right, where Jovan Cvetkovic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can you say approximately what time it was when you stopped for the second time when they were pointing a rifle at you and ...

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: This was at dusk. The sun was setting, it was getting dark. I think it was about 5.00 p.m., it was almost dark because it was even difficult to recognise people's faces. You could only discern silhouettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: At that point, when you got out of the car, when the rifle was pointed at you, did you see Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Including Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. We were all there together, the entire group, we were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. And then you came to this place where Cvetkovic was staying?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What time and was that the last place where you saw Slavko Dokmanovic? At what time was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was. I know that it was almost dark, it was dusk at any rate, and then we stayed there with Cvetkovic, everybody had a drink, whatever was available, we sat there, we talked for a while, and at the same time that is when we parted with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The videotape that I play to you now, do you have a copy?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who gave it to you and when?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Lazarevic gave it to me. I can't remember when he gave it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: '91, '91, but I don't know the exact time because there was no reason for me to remember the exact time because I got it as a souvenir.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And you have this tape until the present day?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If the court required that tape, you could give it to them?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have it as a souvenir, as a valuable memento.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And you could give it to them?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And now I want to complete this once again. I told you that you have to speak the truth because of your oath and also I mentioned that professionally you were a teacher, that you were an educator who teaches children. So this is your -- can you swear saying that you saw Slavko Dokmanovic before your eyes when you left Vukovar and until you reached Sidski Banovci?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Fila's microphone was not on for the last comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, did you finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I have completed. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Williamson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dragisic, whose idea was it to go to Eastern Slavonia from Kladovo on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: The President of the Municipal Assembly, Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And did he approach you and ask you if you wanted to accompany him, or how did it come about that you joined the group?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: He asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Where were these people that you referred to as your former students and athletes, where were they serving in Eastern Slavonia; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know their locations, these villages in the immediate vicinity are not that nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that when you were in Backa Palanka the decision was taken to go to Vukovar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, we agreed -- no, it wasn't a decision that was reached, we simply accommodated our views through a free discussion. This was a voluntary agreement on the part of all of us. It wasn't any kind of decision that was being passed, I mean, for some special reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I'm not trying to indicate that someone ordered you to go there. I'm saying that among all of you, you discussed this and you reached a decision --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: -- to go to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: If your purpose had originally been to go and visit students and athletes, why did you make the change and decide to go to Vukovar instead?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Because I thought that I would see my students, pupils, athletes, the next day, but I thought that this was a unique opportunity to see a town that was devastated. I was really interested in seeing this. So this was the motive that prevailed since I had been given this opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And what was the route that your group took from Backa Palanka to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: That is the road between Backa Palanka and Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I know you're not from the Vukovar area and you have indicated that you weren't familiar with particular names of towns and villages. Do you recall any of the towns and villages that you passed through on the way there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. It was the first time I was travelling in those parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Was it the same route going there as the route that you returned on?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Now, you've said that there were three cars that started out as you left from Backa Palanka to go to Vukovar. What was the order of the cars? Who was first, who was second, who was third leaving from Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, first there was the Mercedes, then the Lada, and then our car -- rather, the car that I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And you said that Mr. Leskovac's car had a flat tyre somewhere along the route; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And do you remember where this was?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No. I remember that a house was there, perhaps it was the beginning of some settlement, but there were some houses, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Was it in the same place where Mr. Cvetkovic was staying, in Sidski Banovci?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And when his car broke down, did he just immediately get into the car, in the Lada, and you continued on your way, or were all of you delayed for some time because of his breakdown?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Very briefly, we just re-packed all of this, Leskovac went and joined them and we continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: So it didn't amount to much of a delay then?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Now, this was your first time ever to be in Vukovar, you said?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And do you recall about what time it was when you arrived at VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Around noon or perhaps around 1.00, sometime after 1.00, 1300 hours and a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: What happened after you arrived? What did you do, if you can just describe for us what happened concerning you after your arrival until the time that you left?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We didn't do anything. We were just watching.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And you were just talking to people that were in the yard?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: To some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Now, earlier the Defence showed you a photograph which was taken at 14.29 and was marked as Exhibit D91. If this could be shown to the witness again, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Right. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And in this photograph, you are standing next to Arkan, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Were you able to ascertain what his purpose was for being there on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: As a director of an elementary school, it didn't concern you in any way to pose for photographs with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I don't understand in what context is this Arkan being mentioned? Does the Prosecutor have some objections against him? Has this person been indicted? I don't know why people wouldn’t want to have their pictures taken with him? Has he been indicted? Why doesn't the Prosecutor tell us. I really have no idea about your sealed indictments, but until he is indicted in public, you cannot qualify a certain person as a person with whom one should not keep company. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Williamson, could you specify the sense of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: That was my follow-up question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: But even in 1991, Mr. Arkan had somewhat of a notorious reputation as a criminal, did he not? Perhaps not as a war criminal but as one with a criminal past in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I know Arkan as a sports fan of the Svezda club, and that's why it was a pleasure for me to have a picture taken with him because he is a major Svezda fan and I am a sportsman myself. I wasn't interested in anything else and I really didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: You indicated that there was this meeting that was taking place at VELEPROMET that all of these people went into the building. Were you aware of what this meeting was about that was inside?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And after the conclusion of the meeting when Mr. Dokmanovic came out, there was no discussion as to what had taken place inside?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: How did it come about that your group eventually left from VELEPROMET?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Because we wanted to see the centre, the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And who suggested that you all go to the centre?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: So again this was just a joint decision made among everyone talking among yourselves?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And who went to the town centre? Who was with you when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: The same group that came in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And when you left from the centre, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Ah, you mean when we left the centre. Sorry, sorry. I didn't understand your question. When we left what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. This was a follow-up question beyond that. I understood that you were in the centre with the same group. I'm now asking when you left the centre, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We set out in the direction of Backa Palanka -- or, rather, further on, to Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And did you return on the same route that you had come in by?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Now, in the statement that you gave and which has been entered as Defence Exhibit 88, you indicate that you left -- after watching the film, you said the film shows us leaving Vukovar at 15.30 by the same road by which we came. Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: If we could show the tape from 15.30 on, if you can just look at it briefly with us? And as you're looking at the tape, if you could indicate to us the point at which you're leaving Vukovar? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We left to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I did not receive a translation. Could you repeat that, please, Mr. Dragisic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: According to the recording, to the best of my recollection, these were the last -- the last scenes when we were leaving Vukovar and moving towards Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And is that -- you're saying that this part, if we can just play it back then perhaps from 15.36 on, and if you can indicate to us where you believe you're leaving Vukovar on that tape?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I really don't know exactly. To the best of my recollection, you know, because I don't know the details, and I didn't really pay much attention to this because I didn't have any reason to pay attention to that, so I don't really know whether it was ten minutes more or five minutes more or afterwards, but this is more or less the kind of information that I can give, that that is when we're leaving town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I'm not trying in any way to trip you up, Mr. Dragisic, I'm just trying to clarify at what point you're referring to in your statement where it shows you leaving, and I understand that these times are approximate. I'm not in any way trying to imply this has to be the exact time. I'm just asking at what point on this tape is it your belief that you left from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I can't say that because I don't remember. Sometime ... I don't know. Forty past 15 or around 1600 hours, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: These buses we have just seen in this very last clip which is indicated at 1542, was that in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I think that was out of Vukovar, as far as I can remember. Yes, yes, it was out of Vukovar at any rate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: We see houses there. Is it in another village or where was it? Again without -- I know you can't say the name of a particular place.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: As long as there were houses, there must have been -- it must have been a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. You cannot see houses anywhere. Houses is plural. On this recording, we see one house, and that is the singular here and anywhere else in the world. So one can see one house, the roof of one house, and that is the right way of phrasing this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Williamson, could you please be so kind as to rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Where is this located, to the best of your knowledge? Is it in a village? Is it in between villages? Is it in between towns? Is it a single house? Were there other houses around?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I don't know, and I cannot give an accurate, concrete answer. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Now, I believe you've testified during examination-in-chief that from the time you left the centre of Vukovar until you stopped for the buses, that you and the group of cars made no turns, no stops, no changes in direction at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We didn't change direction, but we did stop by chance and because of the need, because we were stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Where did you stop between the centre of town and these buses, or did I misunderstand you? Was this the first stop, was for the buses, or was there another stop in between?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Yes, because of the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: So again, just to be absolutely clear, from the time you left the centre of Vukovar until you stopped for the buses, there were no other stops, turns, changes in direction; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: How long were you all stopped for the buses?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Not long. Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Did you get out of the car there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: We didn't all. Some came out, but really, we didn't -- we were there next to one another and we waited and then very shortly after that, we left. We continued on further.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: So some of the people got out, but you yourself did not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. We were car-to-car, next car -- some people maybe came out. We were all together and we maybe commented on it and then later we went on our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you respond to questions whether you went out of the car here or there, do you remember today, after seven years from that event?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO DRAGISIC
utterances.text: Well, of course in any case, I can remember, some details I remember based on what I have just seen, but I probably wouldn't remember a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume there is no objection to the witness being released?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Dragisic, thank you so much for giving evidence in court. You may be released now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (Witness stood down)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, may I ask you who is coming next?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The next witness is called Boris Ivaskovic. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivaskovic, may I ask you to make the solemn declaration, please, read out the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ivaskovic, on December 8th, '97, did you give a statement to the investigator in the office of Fila to investigator Vasic? Would you please look at this statement, tell us whether that is your statement and whether that is your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Statement is marked D93 and the English translation D93A.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The English translation, would you look at the second part, please, that's where the Serbian language statement is.

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's your statement?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Unless there are objections, I move that this be admitted into evidence as D93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Williamson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ivaskovic, did you finish the business school in Belgrade as well as the faculty of philosophy in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The faculty of theology and the business school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where were you employed during your career?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: For five years, I worked as a sales representative in a tourist organisation of Djerdap. After that I worked in radio until the present time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On November 20th, '91, were you a member of the delegation of the assembly of Kladovo, municipality of Kladovo, which visited the war zone?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On November 20th, '91, did you see Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please play the tape, D2, Defence evidence, from the beginning, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the tape and indicate when you see yourself?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The usher please show this photograph to the witness so that he can tell us whether he is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph is marked D94.

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is me on the photograph and driver Rade Ivezic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please run the tape? When you see Slavko Dokmanovic, would you please indicate that for us? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you notice Dokmanovic, please indicate that to us.

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long have you known Mr. Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: I've known -- I saw him earlier when the white fleet sailed between Kladovo, Belgrade, and Vukovar. I know that he lived in Vukovar. Later, I found out that he was the President of the Municipality of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Run the tape, please. Run the tape, please. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you see yourself again, please indicate that to us.

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: This is me on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At this time, I would like the usher to show the photograph to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph is marked D95.

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at another document? Would you please show this to the witness? And to tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D96.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: These are travel orders that I received to travel to visit the reservists as a journalist. This is a usual thing, to get a travel order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you, please, if there are no objections from the Prosecution, I would like the evidence -- the exhibits from 94 to 96 be accepted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Before I move to the next question, could you please tell us what's the meaning of a travel order, when is it issued and so on?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: A travel order means that somebody is being sent on an official trip, he has a business task which is written in the travel orders, and then also to make a report from the war zone. This is a usual thing and it's usually issued a few days before the trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that day, you moved -- you went from Kladovo to Backa Palanka. Why?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: The agreement was to meet with our team that went to the war zone in Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long were you in Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: The group that I was with was in Backa Palanka until 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go from Palanka?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: From Palanka, we went towards Bogojevo Most and then we crossed into Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When was the last time on that day that you saw Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Somewhere around twelve o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Williamson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Your Honour. Cross-examined by.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Ivaskovic, what was your reason going to the Vukovar region on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: In my travel orders, it states that I went as a journalist in order to report from that region because we had our reservists from our area stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who had asked you to go there?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: My newsroom because there were reservists from our municipality, so the newsroom gave me a job as a journalist, gave me a task, assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who did you travel with from Kladovo to Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: In the car that I was in, it was a green Peugeot, there was driver Radoslav Matevic, Radisav Simic, Viselav Maletic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you leave Kladovo and when did you arrive in Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: I only remember that we left in the early morning hours. I can't exactly state what was our departure time, but this was early morning hours. In Backa Palanka, we got there a little before 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you've indicated that at around noon the group split up and that you went across the Bogojevo Bridge to Erdut and the other group went on to Vukovar. Who made the decision as to who would go where?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't go through over the Vukovar but over the Bogojevo Bridge toward Erdut and Dalj, we went to that region in order to visit, as I said earlier, the reservists, and in order to distribute to them what their families sent us. There were sweaters, cigarettes, a little bit of food, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I understand that you went to Erdut and in that direction, but I believe you testified that the other group, including Mr. Dokmanovic, went in another direction, they went off to Vukovar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: They left in a different direction. I didn't know where they were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there any discussion among the people as to who would go to Erdut and who would go with Mr. Dokmanovic's group in the direction of wherever they went?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: We were only told that we are going towards Vukovar, and as a journalist, I recorded a few interesting people for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Whether towards Vukovar, where were you going? Maybe this was a slip of the tongue of the witness. You said you went towards Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: No, we went towards Dalj and Erdut, Dalj and Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And after you left from Backa Palanka, you did not see Mr. Dokmanovic again at any point that day; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him at all. We were in Dalj and Trpinja. At Trpinja, we spent the night there, we slept there, and the next day we came back. I didn't see him any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You did not see him in Trpinja that night?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And did you receive a copy of the videotape which has been shown in court previously marked as Defence Exhibit 2, the one that you have viewed?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I watched that tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And did you receive a copy of that tape in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't get a copy of that videotape because my colleague, Dr. Zoran Jevtovic, my director, had a copy, so I didn't really need one. I saw it once, so I didn't really need to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of Mr. Jevtovic making copies of the tape at that time and distributing them to some of the people who had participated in the trip?

utterances.speaker: BORIS IVASKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was no secret. Anybody who got it and who saw it could make themselves a copy. It was no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I assume the parties will not object to the witness being released? Thank you, Mr. Ivaskovic, for coming here. You may be released now. And we will take a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: --- Resumed at 4.45 p.m. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milivojevic, on 8th of December, '97, did you give a statement to the investigator for the Defence? Is that this statement? Would you please look, if this is your signature on the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Statement is marked D97, English translation D97A.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that your statement? Would you please look at the document, look on the back? That's the English translation. Is that your signature underneath the statement?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I move, unless there are objections, that this be admitted as evidence for the Defence, number 97, English translation 97A.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milivojevic, did you finish technical college?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: On the Djerdap hydroelectric power station.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You were a member of the delegation of the Municipality of Kladovo which visited the war zone on November 20th, '91?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please show the witness the tape and around 9.00, nine and eight minutes, and then in order not to take up time, to move then to 10.39. Okay. Just 9.00. It's okay. When you see yourself, please indicate that to us. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please show the witness this photograph so that the witness can identify it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph is marked D98.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please play the tape further?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And indicate when you see Slavko Dokmanovic on the tape and, of course, when you see yourself.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is me. This is Slavko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. You can stop the tape. When were you in Backa Palanka? On what day?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: The 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 20th of November. Until when were you in Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Until 12.00. We went in the direction of Erdut over the Bogojevo Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At twelve o'clock, did you see Mr. Dokmanovic for the last time?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Milivojevic, you said just as your last statement that you left Backa Palanka around midday on 20th November, 1991, in the direction of Erdut; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Towards -- in the direction of the bridge near Bogojevo, towards Erdut. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Who was with you?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was in the vehicle with Dule Niculovic, the driver, and Dimitrje Vuvucic (phoen).

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was there another car besides the car you were sitting in?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that direction, yes, there was another vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember who were the passengers of that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night that day?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: The 20th? 20th?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: In Trpinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Dokmanovic in Trpinja that night?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So it was the last time you saw Mr. Dokmanovic when you left him in Backa Palanka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MILIVOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. I think there is no objection to the witness being released. Thank you for coming here to give evidence in court. You may be released. (Witness stands down)

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I would like to inform the court and the Prosecution that for the next two witnesses, we don't have written statements, but the investigator of the Prosecution spoke with both of the witnesses in Belgrade during the month of February. That is why we brought them, for that reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So the first one is Mr. Maletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Maletic is the next witness. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please stand and make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, would you please tell us your full name and last name and the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I am Maletic Viselav, father Ratibor, from Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 10th of April in 1945 in Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you finish law school in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I finished law school in 1970 in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about your work career?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: 1971, I started in the Municipal Court in Kladovo until '73 when, after passing the bar exam, I was elected as a judge in the Municipal Court where I was a judge until '87. Then, as I am also from '78 up to the present time, the Public Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of the delegation of the municipality which visited on November 20th, '91, that region?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of that delegation from Kladovo which, on that day, left towards Dalj in order to visit our reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Since it's not in the record that the witness is a Prosecutor in Kladovo -- it does state that he's a Prosecutor but he is actually working as a Prosecutor in Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So are you the Public Prosecutor in Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, when did you leave from Kladovo, if you left from Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: We left from Kladovo early in the morning in a passenger vehicle. There were four of us in the vehicle besides the driver. There was Simic Radisav, then myself, Rade Matovic was the driver, and the journalists, I can't remember the names at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did you get to Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: We got to Backa Palanka around 8.00, 8.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please play the tape for the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you see yourself on the tape, would you please indicate that to us? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's you at nine o'clock and eight minutes?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, nine o'clock and eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please play the tape further.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Next segment of the tape, point to yourself and to Slavko Dokmanovic. Show us Slavko Dokmanovic and yourself.

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: No, we haven't appeared yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Stop the tape, please. Is that you in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's me on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please show the witness the photograph.

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I am on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the photograph and then please say whether it's you on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph is marked D99.

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I would like to have it admitted into evidence as Defence Exhibit 99.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please continue playing the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you see Slavko Dokmanovic, please indicate him.

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: This is Slavko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That will do as far as the tape is concerned. Since when have you known Slavko Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: That is when I first met him. That is when I first met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What were you saying?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: That was the first time we met. We were introduced there in the building of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Until when were you in this room in the Municipality of Backa Palanka?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: We were in that room until around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: As we got out, we went to -- I mean I -- I took this vehicle and went with Simic towards Dalj and the truck did too, and the other group went to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When was the last time that you saw Slavko Dokmanovic on that day?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Sometime after 12.00, when we set out for Dalj. After that, we didn't see each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, could you please look back to the picture we just were shown, D99, please? Can you be shown that picture? You have it in front of you, I see. Do you recognise, Mr. Maletic, the other gentleman on that picture? Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand this question. Are you talking about the photograph I have in front of me?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I know this is Ljuba Tomic, Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And he's a member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
