utterances.text: I know him from Kladovo. We've known each other since we were children. And that was the first time we met. He was a member of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you tell us today what you were discussing with him? You seem to be quite sort of deep into a discussion showing -- maybe you had some papers in front of the two of you. Can you tell us what you were discussing with him?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: As I mentioned to you, we have been friends since childhood. We've known each other since then and we hadn't seen each other for quite some time. So we mostly discussed our families and general affairs; nothing special, nothing specific. We didn't look at any papers. I mean, not in any special way. We were sitting at the table and we were probably looking at some kind of pictures, photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing at that meeting or in general in that area? Do you know his assignment?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: We had an agreement to meet with our vehicles in Backa Palanka so that we could get the right papers and guides to take us further onto the front line. And sometime after we arrived, Ljuba Tomic arrived. Whether he was one of the people who provided these papers for us and made the front line accessible to us, I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You said you were provided with a guide who would lead you through the area. Do you mean a guide who would join you in your car? Was there such a person who guided you around when you continued your way?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I do not remember. No one joined us in our vehicle. It was all of us who were there originally and then the truck went with us too. If there was someone in the truck; that, I do not know. I think that we were simply told what is the route that we were supposed to take and where we were supposed to report because after Dalj, somebody got in touch with us and then we went on with the truck and these packages so that we would distribute them. I mean these parcels.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You said that you knew Mr. Tomic from childhood. Do you know whether he came with you that day or was he in that area prior to the day you met with him?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the beginning of your question. Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You said earlier that you knew Mr. Tomic from childhood; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And he came from Kladovo as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The day we are talking about, 20th of November, 1991, do you have the impression that Mr. Tomic came from Kladovo like you, the same day, or do you have the impression that he was there for quite some time?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was not with us that day. He certainly didn't leave Kladovo that day because we were the only ones who left Kladovo that day in that vehicle and then there was the truck too and the rest of the delegation joined us in Backa Palanka itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: My question was whether Mr. Tomic arrived with you basically, like you for one day, or are you aware whether he was already there, maybe for a month prior to meeting you incidentally, as it may be, during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I don't know how long he was there or whether he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Where did he go, Mr. Tomic, after that meeting; do you know?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either, where he went. As I said, we went towards Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, is he a career officer or a reservist; could you tell us more about his status within the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: He was an active duty officer, military officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know which part of the army or the armed forces Mr. Tomic was, infantry or artillery?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know exactly in which service he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can't you judge that from his uniform, maybe his insignias?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: On these uniforms that were worn, there are no insignia or signs in terms of units, service, et cetera. I mean, that he had then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness please say whether the person we are talking about, did he perhaps wear the uniform of an air force officer?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: No. A regular olive gray-green uniform, just like all other soldiers. That is that uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Without any -- do you perhaps know what an air force uniform looks like?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I do. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe it to us in brief?

utterances.speaker: VISELAV MALETIC
utterances.text: The air force wear blue uniforms and blue insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume there is no objection to the witness being released. Thank you. You are released. (Witness stands down)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I assume we are moving on to our next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Our next witness is Niculovic. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Niculovic, good afternoon. Could you please read out the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness please tell us his full name and surname and his father's name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dusan Niculovic. My father's name is Milutin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th of July, 1947.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where do you live today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: I live in Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Your address?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: Timocka No. 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you employed as a driver at the Djerdap 1 power station in Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've been working there for the past 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You're a driver?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you drive the delegation of the Municipality of Kladovo which went to Backa Palanka on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: I drove a truck with Milivojevic and Rosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could we please play the tape for the witness, the beginning of the tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you see yourself, please tell us that that's you. Could we please have this photograph shown to the witness and could he please indicate what is on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph is marked D100.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: This is where I was sitting, over there in that office in the municipal assembly with the other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I suggest that this be admitted into evidence as Defence Exhibit number 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How long were you in Backa Palanka in the office we just saw?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: In that office, I think until about 12.00. We went out around 12.00, and then we set out for Dalj with a truck that was taking humanitarian aid there to our reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Slavko Dokmanovic on that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him. And until that, I never knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We can continue playing the tape so that the witness could identify ... (Videotape played) Could we please speed up the tape, fast forward until 10.00, approximately? Now could we play the tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you see Mr. Dokmanovic, please tell us so.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: Here he is, Mr. Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you see Mr. Dokmanovic here in this courtroom today? Where is he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: Over there behind you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you last see Mr. Dokmanovic on that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: At 12.00 when we were parting -- when we went towards Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. Niculovic. Why do you think Mr. Dokmanovic was attending that meeting on 20th November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN NICULOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't a meeting. He came there to see us. It wasn't a meeting, you know, like -- you know, as a driver, I was there. You know, it was more sort of like a gathering, not a meeting, a proper meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I assume there is no objection to the witness being released. Thank you. You may be released. (Witness stands down)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, my idea was to bring two more witnesses in, but there's a congress going on in The Hague and there weren't any hotel rooms available, so two people were sharing rooms respectively, and it really didn't make any sense to have three people per room. Therefore, we don't have any further witnesses. There will be coming in on Sunday three more of them -- three more on Monday -- on Monday, three more, and then Slavko Dokmanovic is four, and the expert is five. Those are the people you will be seeing here and the video link, of course, on Monday and Tuesday. However, who does not come to the video link and who does not arrive by Tuesday to the video link, I shall not insist any longer. So the Defence will finish by the end of next week in addition to what we have we saw yesterday. I have a further question, with your permission? This evidence related to possible sentencing, does that mean that an expert can be brought in? Because according to the rules, you are supposed to bear in mind the sentencing policy in Yugoslavia at that period of time. So perhaps in that stage, should I perhaps bring in such a person? Because I do have this kind of intention, to bring in an expert in this kind of penalty policy, as we used to call it, of the SFRY. Would that be the proper time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, it will be quite appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In that case, I shall need two days in June at the most. Really, you know, even God needed seven days to create the world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. No, you're right. So two days in June because we're thinking that the Prosecutor will need two days for the rebuttal witnesses and then one day for the closing statements for both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can certainly try to do that. At this point, since the Defence case is not yet finished, it's a bit premature for us to commit to exactly how many witnesses that we might call. We would certainly do everything we could to try to complete it in June. I think it's in everyone's interests to accomplish that. Just one other point in reference to this. We certainly have no objection to Mr. Fila calling this expert, but we would just ask that we receive a statement from him in advance as to the nature of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. I was going to ask Mr. Fila also about the statement by the expert witness Dr. Petrovic, Vera Petrovic. We have not yet received a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The Registrar has promised me that it will be finished by tomorrow, so you will receive it tomorrow. But in the Serbian language, I have already provided copies. As far as evidence of the Defence is concerned, I want to make this quite clear. All the Defence evidence will be presented by the end of next week. But what we are talking about now is something completely different. I mean, the Prosecutor has no right of rebuttal as far as this particular witness is concerned. This is an expert witness on penalties and sentencing in Yugoslavia. So by the end of next week, the Prosecutor will know exactly what the Defence has done and what the Defence intends to present. Am I clear on this? Do we understand each other on this? I need two days in June for the family of Mr. Dokmanovic, perhaps a friend or two, and that expert witness who is going to tell us about this penalty policy, sentencing policy. That's all. But as far as the evidence provided by the Defence is concerned, I told you that that would be completed by the end of next week, so the Prosecutor will know exactly what they need by then. And, of course, I am going to give Mr. Williamson the statement of that expert when I find this particular expert, because I still haven't found an expert for this, but when I find an expert, of course I'm going to provide the statement of that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just very briefly? I'm not sure that we would agree that we have no right of rebuttal on this issue of sentence. I think that it's -- we have just been informed about this issue, that the court expected evidence of this to be presented during the course of the trial itself; and therefore, if evidence is presented by the Defence, I think we would have the right to rebut that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. Yes. There will be evidence from both parties. Yes. Of course. On the question of sentencing. All right. So we are grateful to Mr. Fila for his promise that he will submit both to the Prosecutor and to the court the statement of the witness expert on the sentencing in the Former Yugoslavia, the judicial practice, which will be of great interest, in any case, for the court, whatever the final decision of the court. I wonder whether I could also ask Mr. Fila about the witness statements of witnesses Miodrag Pavlovic and Radoslav Zlatic, whether we are going to get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I have also handed them in, and I think that we are going to get them next Tuesday. You see, may I remind you of what I said about the Yugoslav army. I had such trouble in convincing at least one person to come in, and I must say that you have a message from the army of Yugoslavia that whatever the court wishes to have, according to the rules, if you need a document, that they're going to give it to you. But they won't give it to me because it says "Confidential." But if the court asks for it, then the head of the legal service of the JNA, Colonel Ristic, he said that he will give you whatever you ask for, but he won't give me anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you for this information, which is most gratifying, but we were never told that the authorities in Belgrade, the military authorities in Belgrade, would give us whatever we would ask for. Of course, if you're interested in any document, you could put in a request to us and we would be most happy to send this as a request from the court to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just very quickly. I don't know if Mr. Fila is aware of this. We yesterday received a statement of Mr. Pavlovic, so I believe the translation of that statement is completed. The other one we have not yet received, so I suppose it's still in the process of being translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Again, turning to this question of military documents, of military information --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I sent Pavlovic's statement in Serbian. You got a copy in English? When did you manage to get that? I mean, it is following -- Mr. Pavlovic is a colonel of the JNA, and in his statement -- I mean, when he testifies before the Honourable Court, he is going to invoke certain documents, and I wanted him to bring in these documents to show them to you. And you know that according to our rules, you cannot just talk; you have to show documents in order to corroborate this. Well, he won't be able to get these documents otherwise. Only if you ask them will you be able to get them. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. That's why I'm asking you whether you could submit to the court a request for those documents which you are interested in, and tomorrow we can send a formal request to the army, the relevant authorities in Belgrade, so that they can provide us with those documents as soon as possible. Ideally, it would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It is better for him to say what are the documents when he testifies on Wednesday and Thursday, and then we are going to request them and then they will arrive before June because then we are going to see what is of interest. Perhaps there is something that the Prosecutor may find interesting too, but I don't know if they are going to keep their word. I am just telling you what they have told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would suggest that perhaps Mr. Fila talk to the witness beforehand and find out which documents are involved because I think if he's going to submit these, we would want the gentleman to verify them in court before we would have no objection to them being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, so I go back to my proposal, my suggestion, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Try. Try. I would have to see them first, but they won't let me see them. That's the problem. Because -- perhaps we know what it's all about also. It pertains to the situation in '90 and '91, attacks on JNA barracks, the ethnic structure of the JNA, how many different ethnic groups there were and how many members of each group, Serbs, Croats, Bosnians, et cetera. That is what they say is a military secret and that they cannot disclose it to me. And that's all. I mean, that is the point. That is the core of the matter, because Mr. Williamson put questions about this ethnic structure of the JNA in the period that is relevant to this indictment. Witness Pavlovic is going to speak about it. He does have figures about that, and he can present them. But only you can ask for an official document, an official report on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That is the core of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Again, my suggestion, which was supported by the Prosecutor for other reasons, probably is the best one, but it's not realistic to expect that they will provide by next week all these documents. So I wonder whether we could go about this matter as follows: The witness will come here to testify and will indicate what sort of documents we would need. Then we will send a formal request to the military authorities in Belgrade; and if they send these documents, then in June they may or may not be admitted in evidence after they are shown to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that would be fine. We wouldn't want to commit ourselves at this point until we have seen the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be recalled in June to identify the documents and to verify them at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That's right. We can recall him. Because I didn't see them. It's a report. For example, they tell me that it was sent to the Tribunal God-knows-when, this report that is being translated. Perhaps it is in the OTP. I don't know. They said that they sent it way back. But whether they sent it, I don't know. I cannot claim that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We will check all that next week. One final issue: The Prosecutor may remember that some time ago we asked the Prosecution to provide the court and, of course, the Defence, with colour stills of Mr. Dokmanovic taken from the videotape. I wonder whether we could get stills in colour of Mr. Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have some stills. I would have to check on the exact status of that. I'm not sure if we have completed it and have all of the stills that the court was asking for, but I'll certainly make every attempt to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: In particular, stills from the tape we saw today and yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: From Defence Exhibit 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Yes. We will check and see what we can find.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Do you think we could get all those documents by next Monday? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I will see. I know that we have had some problem, and I assume that it has affected the first floor as well. We understand that they do not have paper for printing, and so this also includes the appropriate paper for printing photographs. So I'm not sure if that situation has been resolved in its entirety, but I'll endeavour to find out this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Any other question or issue to be discussed? All right. So we will resume our hearings on Monday, next Monday, at 9.30. Yes. So we will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: at 5.30 p.m. to be resumed Monday, 25 May, 1998 at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
